seo.title: Toys R Us: brand film generated with Sora - backlash over the AI ad (2024)
seo.meta_description: In June 2024, Toys R Us aired a brand film at Cannes made with Sora. The rendering, judged soulless, tipped brand sentiment negative.
seo.resume_citable: In June 2024, Toys R Us unveiled at Cannes a brand film generated mainly with OpenAI's Sora; brand sentiment fell to 3.4% positive against 53.4% negative after airing.

faq.q: What went wrong with the 2024 Toys R Us ad?
faq.a: The brand film, produced mainly with Sora, showed an inconsistent rendering (the child changes appearance from shot to shot) and was rejected as soulless by the public and the creative community. Brand sentiment tipped negative.

faq.q: Is AI-generated video a doomed pattern?
faq.a: No. The failure is about this 2024 execution (unpolished rendering, foregrounding the process on an emotional subject), not about the category, which is advancing fast and already serves in supporting production.

objectif_business: Get the brand talked about with a film honoring its founder Charles Lazarus, positioning itself as a pioneer of AI video production.
description: In June 2024, Toys R Us presented at the Cannes Lions festival a brand film of about 66 seconds made mainly with Sora, OpenAI's video generation tool. The spot tells the childhood of Charles Lazarus and the dream said to have inspired the brand and its giraffe mascot. The rendering carries the typical markers of the generative: the child changes appearance from shot to shot, the texture is smooth and artificial. The reaction from the creative community and the public was immediate and hostile, the ad being called soulless. The brand defended the choice rather than pulling the film.

resultats.metrique: Negative brand sentiment, before then after airing
Official brand response, cutting-edge technology invoked
Dominant creative criticism, rendering seen as AI filler

niveau_preuve.justification: Established press (Forbes, eMarketer) and a sentiment-measurement tool (Marketing-Interactive) report the brand, the tool, and the response from its marketing leadership by name. No financial or legal document, hence C.

stack_technique.detail: OpenAI's text-to-video model used to generate most of the film's shots; in 2024, it did not hold a character's consistency between shots.
The publisher of the Sora model used to produce the brand film.
Editing, music, and corrections done by the creative team; tools not publicly named.

post_mortem.ce_qui_s_est_passe: In June 2024, Toys R Us unveiled at Cannes a brand film produced mainly with Sora. The spot is conceived as a tribute to founder Charles Lazarus. From the moment it aired, creatives and internet users attacked the artificial rendering and the choice not to bring in professionals. The brand's sentiment measurement flipped from neutral to negative within days. The brand kept the film and defended its technology bet.
post_mortem.raison_echec: The rejection comes from two documented things: an inconsistent visual rendering (the child changes look between shots, the smooth texture typical of the generative) and a principled rejection by the creative community of an ad that replaces human work with AI. The very subject of the spot, a child's limitless imagination, made the contrast with a machine rendering even more poorly received.
post_mortem.cout_estime: Reputational cost: a measured swing of sentiment to the negative, unfavorable international press coverage. No direct financial cost published.
post_mortem.signaux_avant_coureurs: Inferred: in 2024 the Sora tool did not hold a character's consistency across multiple shots, which was already known to technical teams. Airing a rendering carrying the visible artifacts of the generative, on an emotional subject, before an audience of creatives at Cannes, stacked the conditions for rejection.
post_mortem.lecons_avec_recul: Inferred: AI video generation can serve in production (previsualization, moodboards, filler shots) without being exposed raw as the final film of a major brand. The 2024 public judges harshly an ad that shows its AI seams on emotional content. A discreet, controlled use is better than a communication stunt about having generated everything.
post_mortem.le_pattern_reste_il_valide: Inferred: yes, the AI-generated video pattern remains valid and is advancing fast. The failure condemns this execution (unpolished 2024 rendering, poorly chosen subject, foregrounding the process), not the category. The reception question is moving: what shocked in 2024 will be judged differently as quality rises and the use becomes commonplace.

prerequis_orga: quality control of the rendering before airing
replication.premiere_etape: Define where AI video really serves (previz, filler shots) and decide upfront whether the final rendering can withstand being exposed raw to the target audience.

statut_vivant.note: A backlash case without withdrawal: Toys R Us defended the film instead of deleting it. The episode remains a reference point on public rejection of a fully AI ad.

transposable_ue.note: The risk is identical in Europe: a mass-market brand airing a fully AI-generated ad exposes itself to the same reputational rejection. The AI Act requires labeling synthetic content (transparency obligation), and misleading-advertising rules apply if the rendering does not match the product. The problem here is not legal but reputational: the public associates generative AI with giving up on creative work.
